author: yassinyl
description: iVentoy is a PXE network boot server that allows computers to boot and install operating systems over the network using ISO images.

tips.before_install:
IMPORTANT - NETWORK CONFIGURATION

iVentoy uses a macvlan network and requires a dedicated
IP address on your local network.

The macvlan network is created automatically during
installation.

IMPORTANT:

Before installing iVentoy, check the network settings
in the Docker Compose configuration.

The following values must match your local network:

- parent: your physical LAN interface
- subnet: your local IPv4 subnet
- gateway: your router IP
- ipv4_address: an unused IP address on your LAN
- ip_range: an unused IP range on your LAN

Example:

parent: eth0

subnet: 192.168.1.0/24

gateway: 192.168.1.1

ipv4_address: 192.168.1.170

ip_range: 192.168.1.160/28

Make sure that the selected iVentoy IP address is not
already used by another device.

IMPORTANT:

Port 26000 is published for the Web interface.

The remaining iVentoy PXE services use the macvlan
network directly.

If your network configuration is different from the
example above, change the macvlan network settings
before installation.
tips.after_install:
IMPORTANT - COMPLETE iVentoy SETUP

After the installation is complete:

1. Download the latest Linux Free Edition from:

https://github.com/ventoy/PXE/releases

2. Extract the downloaded archive.

3. Open the extracted "data" directory.

4. Copy these two files:

iventoy.dat
mac.db

5. Copy both files to:

/DATA/AppData/iVentoy/data/

The final structure must be:

/DATA/AppData/iVentoy/data/iventoy.dat
/DATA/AppData/iVentoy/data/mac.db

6. Restart the iVentoy container.

After restarting, open the Web interface using:

http://<iVentoy-IP>:26000

If your router already provides DHCP, use iVentoy
ProxyNet mode.

Do NOT enable iVentoy Internal DHCP.
